lcd.title: Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI) of the Lumbar Spine

indications.criterion: Documented failure of at least 6 weeks of conservative therapy, including physical therapy, nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory medications, or activity modification, without clinically significant improvement.
Persistent neurological symptoms that correlate with imaging: motor deficit, dermatomal sensory loss, reflex changes, or bowel/bladder dysfunction suggestive of cauda equina syndrome.
The clinical presentation must plausibly correlate with lumbar pathology; pain alone without neurological or functional findings is insufficient.
The imaging is ordered to plan a specific surgical or interventional procedure, or to rule out a surgical lesion when conservative measures have failed.

limitations.limitation: Repeat lumbar MRI within 12 months of a prior study requires documentation of a new neurologic deficit, significant clinical change, or post-operative evaluation. Routine surveillance MRI is not covered.
Routine screening MRI for nonspecific low back pain without neurological findings is not a covered indication.
MRI performed solely for administrative purposes (employment physicals, insurance underwriting, legal proceedings) is not covered.
